name: Patio heater

combustion.note: The maker of a 48,000 BTU/h (14.1 kW) tower heater warns it makes CO that can kill in a camper, tent, car or home, and allows it only outdoors, under a roof only with the sides largely open. Electric patio heaters in this record burn nothing.

comps.spec: Propane in a 20 lb (9 kg) cylinder hidden in the base, often part full — never burn a propane heater indoors
Refillable propane cylinder (the 20 lb tank in North America), in the base

comps.loc: At the burner, beside the pilot

comps.spec: Gas control valve with flame-safety and anti-tilt cutoff
Shiny aluminium or steel reflector hood, about 80 cm across — reflector panels for a solar oven
Steel or stainless pole, about 2 m
Infrared halogen or carbon lamps, 1.5–2 kW (electric models)

notes:
Restaurants often keep a row of heaters, each hiding a cylinder in its base. Check the shed or cage out back for spares.

Gas ones are outdoors only. They give off carbon monoxide that can kill in a camper, tent, car or home (Master Forge DG48PMHMF), and Quebec's building authority says never to bring one indoors for heat in a power cut (RBQ propane). For one 48,000 BTU/h model the maker allows use under a roof only in a partial enclosure of no more than two walls, with open wall area as its manual sets out, and keeps combustible material at least 66 cm (26 in) from the sides and back and 81 cm (32 in) from the ceiling (Master Forge DG48PMHMF). CSA 2.37 / ANSI Z83.26 is the joint standard for gas-fired outdoor infrared patio heaters; the 2007 edition the SCC lists is cancelled and was replaced by the 2014 one (SCC Z83.26).

sources.title: Master Forge DG48PMHMF: Master Forge (LF, LLC), 48,000-BTU propane patio heater DG48PMHMF, owner's manual
RBQ propane: Régie du bâtiment du Québec, Safety advice: propane use

SCC Z83.26: Standards Council of Canada standards database, ANSI Z83.26-2007/CSA 2.37-2007 (R2012), Gas-fired outdoor infrared patio heaters (scope; this edition cancelled, superseded by the 2014 edition)
